walkthrough:
Form the composite function $fg(x)$ and equate to 1:
$$fg(x) = f\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) = 2 - 3\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) = 1$$

Solve for $x$ in the range $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ (to 3 significant figures):
$$x = 2 \times 1.2310 \approx 2.4619 \approx 2.46 \text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } \approx 0.784\pi)$$

hints: Starts at $(0,-1)$, peaks at $(\pi, 5)$, ends at $(2\pi, -1)$.
walkthrough:
Identify the key features of the curve $y = 2 - 3\cos x$ on $[0, 2\pi]$:
$$\text{Starts at } (0, \, -1), \quad \text{Reaches maximum at } (\pi, \, 5), \quad \text{Ends at } (2\pi, \, -1)$$
Sketch one complete cycle of the inverted cosine curve with amplitude 3 and vertical shift $+2$, ensuring the curve turns smoothly at its endpoints and maximum.
